blindSummary:
This country is very safe for transgender visitors. A 2022 reform of personal/family law modernised the legal framework (unified civil marriage plus legal gender recognition provisions); the equality ministry now obliges all companies to maintain sexual & gender-based harassment protocols. A regional LGBTI-rights organisation records only three bias-motivated incidents in the most recent annual review — a tiny absolute number reflecting a small, safe, tourism-dependent country.

No traveler-facing concerns: no bathroom laws, no border issues (open border with two neighbouring states; although the country sits outside the regional visa-free area, there are no document-gender checks), high social tolerance in practice despite a conservative religious history. Gaps: anti-discrimination coverage of gender identity is recent & shallower than in larger neighbouring states; hate-crime law is generic rather than SOGI-specific.
blindOutOfScope: Religious influence on family law is resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2024 (covering 2023), chapter on this country: the 2022 personal/family-law reform entered into force in February 2023, introducing legal gender recognition. A newspaper opinion piece linking trans identities to mental illness was removed after protest, with a public apology. A local trans-rights organisation met the health ministry on gender-affirming-care protocols following the 2022 regulatory changes; microaggressions were reported but rarely to authorities, attributed to fear.

Regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2026 (covering 2025), chapter on this country: police record an average of two to three bias-motivated incidents per month; the local trans-rights organisation calls for a formal hate-crime registration system. In October a decree on trans-specific healthcare entered into force: HRT via the social security system from age 16, surgery from 18, plus consultation coverage for under-16s. New workplace harassment protocols were criticised for not explicitly addressing gender diversity or trans-specific harassment.

Independent travel-safety index (2023): ranks 203 countries for LGBTQ+ travel safety based on laws plus international sources; also publishes a global transgender-rights index - a comparative travel-safety framework covering this country among all countries.

NOTE: the underlying international LGBT-rights page was for this country, but the fetched content displayed a regional peer's overview (site template error at fetch time); this country's overview (March 2026) covers its protections - marriage equality, gender-identity anti-discrimination law, plus trans healthcare rights.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (Sept 2023): this country's head of government came out as gay, saying he had never hidden it & hoping it shows young people that anyone can reach the highest office; during his premiership the country legalised same-sex marriage, introduced gender identity/expression anti-discrimination laws, as well as advancing trans rights.

Legal-directory site's country laws page: age of consent 16 (under a penal-code provision); a registered-partnership law since March 2005 gave same-sex partners some marriage rights; discrimination prohibited since 2005 - dated but specific legal reference.
blindLocalsOnly: Legal gender recognition provisions exist under the 2022 personal/family-law reform; the anti-discrimination & hate-crime gaps are resident-facing.
blindTangential: Civil marriage was unified under the 2022 law — relevant to trans visitors travelling with a partner, not to solo travellers.
